To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we cloned and sequenced DNA fragments from the genome of P. falciparu containing repetitive regions that are homologous to a synthetic oligonucleotide consisting of histidine-codon repeats.
the repetitive sequences are conserved and that the two reading frames are conserved in the three strains studied, but not in P. falcipalrum var. berghei and P. vivax.

we have identified two open reading frames in a repetitive sequence of P. falciparium that could code for histidine-rich and aspartic acid-rich proteins, respectively, and that these sequences are highly conserved among different isolates of the parasite.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning, sequencing and characterization of DNA fragments containing repetitive sequences potentially coding for small histidine-rich proteins.
the identification of histidine-rich proteins in P. falciparam and their possible involvement in merozoite invasion of erythrocytes.
histidine-rich protein genes of P. falcifarum and the results are discussed with respect to the potential use of these proteins as vaccine candidates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sequences are coding for a histidine-rich protein and that the aspartic acid-containing protein is a pseudogene, although it is not excluded that it could be expressed.
the DNA fragments sequenced contain repetitive sequences coding for histidine- and aspartic acid-rich proteins.
the sequences are not coding for histidine rich protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified two genes in P. falciparam that are potentially coding for histidin-rich proteins.
the repetitive regions of the P. falciparium histidine-rich protein gene family are highly conserved in different P. falcipuram strains.
we cloned and sequenced DNA fragments of P. falcidarum which contain repetitive regions very homolgous to histidine codons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have cloned and sequenced a repetitive DNA fragment from P. falciparu m.
the histidine-rich protein sequences are very repetitive and are present at least in two copies in the P. falciparu m genome, and are conserved between different strains.
we identified two genes that may code for proteins with histidine-rich repeats and aspartic acid repeats.
